messages.subject: Exploratory bacterial-cellulose biotube concept: long-fiber keratin + chitin + placental ECM
messages.body_verbatim:
Dear Prof. Vignolini,

I am writing to share a small, evidence-gated materials concept that may overlap with your 2026 work on bulk 3D bacterial-cellulose composites and oxygen-enabled growth.

The core idea is to form a bacterial-cellulose filament/tube in an oxygen-accessible tubular mold around three distinct reinforcement phases:

- intact, naturally shed domestic-cat vibrissae as high-aspect-ratio keratin fibers (strictly no plucking/cutting),

- characterized shrimp-derived chitin as a dispersed secondary phase, and

- a separate institutional-only branch using decellularized human placental ECM as a collagen/fibronectin/laminin/GAG scaffold.

The hypothesis is not that these materials are already proven to reinforce BC. The project explicitly keeps the key gates open: oxygen access, BC identity, fiber/matrix interface, chitin distribution, ECM retention, matched controls, and mechanical testing. A previous informal tubular SCOBY experiment produced a cellulose-like filament rather than a flat pellicle, but we preserve that only as an observation until material identity is confirmed.

Relevant machine-readable notes:

https://github.com/Hawkar-usls/janus-meta-registry/blob/main/data/JANUS-SCOBY-VIBRISSA-CHITIN-BIOTUBE-2026-08-20-v1.0.json

https://github.com/Hawkar-usls/janus-meta-registry/blob/main/data/JANUS-XY-PLACENTA-MILK-SCOBY-FULL-REVERSE-GATE-2026-08-20-v1.0.json

https://github.com/Hawkar-usls/janus-meta-registry/blob/main/data/JANUS-FELINE-NATURALLY-SHED-VIBRISSA-CHEMISTRY-2026-08-20-v1.0.json

If this overlaps with experiments your group could evaluate, even as a simple negative/feasibility test, I would be very happy for the idea and data to be useful. If another group is a better fit, a referral would also be greatly appreciated.

Human milk or placental tissue are not proposed as uncontrolled home-culture materials; any human-derived branch is intended only for appropriate institutional ethics/biosafety handling, preferably as decellularized ECM first.

Best regards,

Hawkar

Hawkar-usls / SCOBY-D0 / JANUS Meta Registry

messages.subject: BC tubular-mold follow-up: naturally shed keratin-fiber + chitin reinforcement concept
messages.body_verbatim:
Dear Dr. Foresti and Dr. Cerrutti,

Your work on biosynthesized bacterial-cellulose tubes in cylindrical oxygen-permeable molds is directly relevant to an experimental materials concept I would like to share.

The proposed architecture is a BC filament/tube grown in situ around:

- longitudinal or gently twisted intact feline vibrissae collected only after natural shedding (high-aspect-ratio keratin fibers), and

- characterized shrimp-derived chitin as a dispersed secondary phase.

A separate later branch considers decellularized human placental ECM as a collagen-rich scaffold, but only under institutional ethics/biosafety conditions. The immediate clean gate is the non-human BC + vibrissa + chitin tube.

The project is intentionally claim-bounded. The major unresolved gates are oxygen delivery along the tube, continuous BC identity, fiber pull-out/interface behavior, chitin sedimentation/distribution, wet-state mechanics, and comparison against BC-only / chitin-only / vibrissa-only controls.

Machine-readable protocol/reverse audit:

https://github.com/Hawkar-usls/janus-meta-registry/blob/main/data/JANUS-SCOBY-VIBRISSA-CHITIN-BIOTUBE-2026-08-20-v1.0.json

messages.subject: Possible extension of BC/collagen “biological suturing” to natural long-fiber + placental-ECM composites
messages.body_verbatim:
Dear Prof. Ding and Prof. Zhang,

I am sharing an exploratory materials concept inspired in part by your 2026 bacterial-cellulose/collagen work using in-situ “biological suturing.”

The proposed architecture is a tubular or filamentary bacterial-cellulose matrix grown around multiple natural reinforcement scales:

- intact domestic-cat vibrissae collected only after natural shedding, used as long keratin fibers;

- characterized shrimp-derived chitin as a dispersed secondary phase;

- and, in a separate institutional-only branch, decellularized human placental ECM as a collagen/fibronectin/laminin/GAG scaffold.

The central question is whether growing BC can physically interweave these phases strongly enough to create a measurable composite effect, rather than simple inclusion or surface adhesion. The reverse audit therefore keeps the following gates open: fiber/matrix load transfer, chitin distribution, ECM retention, continuous BC identity, wet-state mechanics, and matched controls.

Relevant records:

https://github.com/Hawkar-usls/janus-meta-registry/blob/main/data/JANUS-SCOBY-VIBRISSA-CHITIN-BIOTUBE-2026-08-20-v1.0.json

https://github.com/Hawkar-usls/janus-meta-registry/blob/main/data/JANUS-XY-PLACENTA-MILK-SCOBY-FULL-REVERSE-GATE-2026-08-20-v1.0.json

https://github.com/Hawkar-usls/janus-meta-registry/blob/main/data/SCOBY-D1-EXOGENOUS-CHITIN-ARMOUR-v1.1.json

I would be very glad if the concept or data are useful for a feasibility screen in your laboratory. Even a clean negative result on adhesion or reinforcement would be highly informative. If another collaborator in your network is better positioned to test such an in-situ BC composite, I would greatly appreciate a referral.

No human placental tissue is proposed for uncontrolled culture; that branch is intended only as decellularized ECM handled under appropriate institutional protocols.

Best regards,

Hawkar

messages.subject: Decellularized human placental ECM as a scaffold phase for bacterial-cellulose composite growth
messages.body_verbatim:
Dear Dr. Mathapati,

I am writing because your work on human placental extracellular-matrix hydrogels is highly relevant to a materials hypothesis we have been developing around bacterial cellulose (BC).

The cleanest proposed branch is not raw placenta. It is to use decellularized placental ECM as a collagen/fibronectin/laminin/GAG-rich scaffold and ask whether a growing BC network can physically interweave and reinforce it in situ. A separate non-human reinforcement branch combines BC with naturally shed feline vibrissae (long keratin fibers; strictly no plucking/cutting) and characterized shrimp-derived chitin.

The project explicitly treats fetal sex as a covariate rather than a claimed performance determinant: placental fetal compartments are XX/XY and sex-associated transcriptomic/epigenomic differences are real, but whether any relevant ECM difference survives decellularization and changes BC formation is completely open and would require direct matched measurement.

Materials/reverse-audit records:

https://github.com/Hawkar-usls/janus-meta-registry/blob/main/data/JANUS-XY-PLACENTA-MILK-SCOBY-FULL-REVERSE-GATE-2026-08-20-v1.0.json

https://github.com/Hawkar-usls/janus-meta-registry/blob/main/data/JANUS-FETAL-SEX-HUMAN-MILK-Y-MICROCHIMERISM-GATE-2026-08-20-v1.0.json

https://github.com/Hawkar-usls/janus-meta-registry/blob/main/data/JANUS-SCOBY-VIBRISSA-CHITIN-BIOTUBE-2026-08-20-v1.0.json

The key experimental questions are simply whether placental dECM remains structurally identifiable during/after BC growth, whether BC physically interlocks with the retained ECM, and whether any mechanical or wet-state property changes survive matched controls.

If this is relevant to your Biomaterials Laboratory, I would be very happy for you to use or test the idea. If another group at THSTI is a better fit, a referral would be sincerely appreciated.

Any human-derived work is intended only under institutional ethics, biosafety, donor-consent and material-handling procedures; I am not proposing uncontrolled culture of raw human tissue.

Best regards,

Hawkar

Hawkar-usls / SCOBY-D0 / JANUS Meta Registry

messages.subject: Research question from SCOBY-D0: milk fermentation as a materials-forming BC gate
messages.body_verbatim:
Dear Prof. Trząskowska,

I am reaching out because your published work on applying SCOBY/kombucha cultures to fermented milk is directly relevant to an unusual materials-science branch of our open SCOBY-D0 research.

We are not pursuing a food product. The question is whether a milk-based environment can alter bacterial-cellulose formation, matrix chemistry or composite behavior in a controlled research setting. A further human-derived branch concerns donor human milk and decellularized placental ECM, but only under proper institutional ethics/biosafety conditions; raw placenta + human milk + mixed SCOBY is explicitly treated as too confounded for an uncontrolled experiment.

The materials architecture under consideration combines:

- bacterial cellulose formed in a tubular geometry,

- naturally shed feline vibrissae as long keratin fibers (strictly no plucking/cutting),

- characterized shrimp-derived chitin,

- and, separately, decellularized placental ECM as a collagen-rich scaffold.

The main question for your expertise is whether the milk/SCOBY branch should be expected to shift the microbial ecology and BC yield/structure enough to justify a controlled comparison, and which measurements would best distinguish cellulose formation from ordinary milk coagulation or mixed biomass.

Relevant records:

https://github.com/Hawkar-usls/janus-meta-registry/blob/main/data/JANUS-SCOBY-BOY-MILK-VIBRISSA-CHITIN-GATE-2026-08-20-v1.0.json

https://github.com/Hawkar-usls/janus-meta-registry/blob/main/data/JANUS-XY-PLACENTA-MILK-SCOBY-FULL-REVERSE-GATE-2026-08-20-v1.0.json

https://github.com/Hawkar-usls/janus-meta-registry/blob/main/data/JANUS-SCOBY-VIBRISSA-CHITIN-BIOTUBE-2026-08-20-v1.0.json

If this question is scientifically interesting to your group, I would be delighted for the project data to be useful. A suggestion of a laboratory better equipped for the human-milk or BC-materials side would also be greatly appreciated.

Best regards,

Hawkar

messages.subject: Re: Possible extension of BC/collagen “biological suturing” to natural long-fiber + placental-ECM composites
messages.reply_new_text_verbatim:
Dear Prof. Ding and Prof. Zhang,

A brief computational addendum to my previous note may be relevant to your BC/collagen “biological suturing” work.

Alongside the materials-side JANUS gates, I maintain an explicitly upstream-attributed working copy of Tranception, the protein-fitness prediction framework of Notin et al. (ICML 2022):

https://github.com/Hawkar-usls/tranception

Official upstream:

https://github.com/OATML-Markslab/Tranception

I do not claim authorship of the base Tranception research or implementation; my repository is preserved as an upstream-derived working/reference copy.

The possible use in this project is narrow but potentially useful: before committing wet-lab effort to engineered Komagataeibacter variants, Tranception could serve as a candidate-ranking layer for protein-sequence variants in the bacterial-cellulose synthesis/assembly machinery—for example BcsA/BcsB/BcsC/BcsD or relevant accessory proteins. The intended workflow would be:

protein variant space → Tranception ranking → small experimentally testable candidate set → BC yield/morphology/interface/mechanics measurements → JANUS forward/reverse causal audit.

The score would be treated only as a prioritization signal, never as proof that a variant improves cellulose production or composite mechanics.

I thought this may be particularly relevant to your group because your 2026 work already demonstrates an in-situ fermentation architecture in which collagen becomes interwoven with the growing BC network. If useful, I would be very happy for your team to reuse the materials records and the computational reference layer, or to redirect the idea to a colleague working on Komagataeibacter engineering.

Best regards,

Hawkar
